definitions.explanation: A colorful bell pepper, typically red, yellow, or orange. In Japanese, パプリカ specifically refers to the thick-fleshed, sweet varieties imported or grown for salads and cooking, distinguishing them from the thinner-walled ピーマン.

examples.japanese: サラダに{赤|あか}いパプリカを{入|い}れた。
examples.english: I added red bell pepper to the salad.

examples.japanese: パプリカはピーマンより{甘|あま}くて{食|た}べやすい。
examples.english: Bell peppers are sweeter and easier to eat than green peppers.

examples.japanese: {黄色|きいろ}いパプリカと{赤|あか}いパプリカを{使|つか}うと{料理|りょうり}が{華|はな}やかになる。
examples.english: Using yellow and red bell peppers makes the dish look more colorful.

notes:
USAGE:
In Japanese, パプリカ and ピーマン refer to different things. ピーマン is the smaller, thinner-walled green pepper common in Japanese cooking. パプリカ refers to the larger, thicker, sweeter varieties (typically red, yellow, or orange). Both are types of bell pepper in English.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- パプリカの{肉詰|にくづ}め (stuffed bell pepper)
- パプリカパウダー (paprika powder — the spice)
- {赤|あか}パプリカ / {黄|き}パプリカ (red / yellow bell pepper)
